Too bad they overlooked the fact that it's not just a city builder. The best way to describe the Anno games is that they're resource strategy games with city building elements. Like Civilization (but not as detailed) meets SimCity (but not as detailed). It tries to offer both sides of the spectrum and surprisingly does a pretty good job of it. You don't have the range of military units to deploy and a lot of the city building elements are simplified but as the reviewer found out, it was still enjoyable.

Now imagine playing Civ while setting yourself up so that the enemy would never attack you. How fast and dull would the progression be? You can't exclude a big aspect of the game and then say it has no replay value. Try playing the whole game before making that judgment.

I think a game reviewer can do a better job of first understanding what they're supposed to be playing and reviewing based on that instead of deciding they know better than the developer what kind of game it is. Both routes might lead them to the conclusion that they're not fully happy with the game, but at least the first option wouldn't have the embarrassing backlash for them.
